evidence_summary: KCNH2 is the pore-forming alpha subunit of hERG/Kv11.1 and potassium channels function as tetrameric channel assemblies; prior KCNJ2 homotetramer AF3 worked well, and local planning replaced weak KCNH2-KCNE2 with homotetramer.
support_sources: UniProt Q12809; prior local pilot_v2 planning; RCSB/PDB hERG structural context
caveat: Full-length homotetramer is 4636 residues and near the practical server ceiling; no membrane or voltage state.

partner: KCNH2 PAS/PAC with CNBHD intramolecular regulatory pair
evidence_summary: KCNH2 has annotated N-terminal PAS/PAC domains and a cNMP-binding/CNBHD region. A split-domain job tests intramolecular regulatory packing in a compact, interpretable way.
support_sources: UniProt Q12809 domain annotations; RCSB/PDB PAS/CNBHD structural support
caveat: This is same-protein domain-domain context, not an external binding partner.

evidence_summary: UniProt reports KCNE2 associates with KCNH2/HERG to form IKr context, and Reactome maps both to repolarization pathways. However, the prior full-length KCNH2-KCNE2 AF3 result was not interface-usable.
support_sources: UniProt Q12809; UniProt Q9Y6J6; Reactome R-HSA-1296072/R-HSA-5576890/R-HSA-5576893; prior AF3_PILOTV1_REVIEW_KCNH2_KCNE2 QC
caveat: Do not promote KCNE2 features unless a rerun/redesign produces acceptable interface confidence.

evidence_summary: KCNH2 may form a stable complex with KCNE1, but KCNE1 is primarily the KCNQ1/IKs partner in this project and not first-pass KCNH2.
caveat: Held to avoid overexpanding channel auxiliary jobs.

evidence_summary: These proteins relate to KCNH2 trafficking, maturation, or degradation. They may matter biologically but are not clean channel-interface AF3 targets for this first pass.
caveat: Potential future trafficking/regulatory analysis, not primary variant interface features.
